status: Geometry review prototype; not released for manufacture.
assembly: Bench-fit the bearings and spacers before installing the motors.
Install the hip hub, three metal tie sleeves and knee stator plate; verify actuator thread engagement and clamp preload separately.
Install the pushrod bushings, shoulder screws and captured nuts with the shells open.
Seat each shin bearing in its complete circular bore. Close the shin halves around the spacer and metal clamp sleeves.
Fit the shin between the thigh bearing stops, insert the knee axle sleeve and through-bolt, then close the thigh.
For bearing service, remove the knee axle and open the two structural halves. Use the rear extraction holes to press on the outer race.
limits: Printed strength, fatigue, motor heat, clamp preload, actual press fits and accumulated tolerances remain unqualified.
Metal parts need wall/pocket optimization and a supplier tool-access review before CNC ordering.
The nominal foot and motor envelopes are retained; their final retention and wiring details require hardware selection.
reuse_basis: All limb geometry and assembly placements are identical to the audited source.
sensor_assembly: Drill and deburr the two 4.4 mm crossmember holes, or manufacture the revised metal part.
Fit the cradle with two M4 x20 socket-head screws, flat washers and accessible nuts below the crossmember.
Insert four M3 nuts through the open underside of the cradle. Route cables aft around the crossmember, with a disconnect and service slack.
Lower the hood onto its four lands and fit four M3 x20 socket-head screws from above. The lidar does not cover these access holes.
The main body cover and sensor hood lift independently. Remove the hood before accessing the two cradle mounting screws.
sensor_limits: The selected lidar mounting pattern and camera cartridge retention remain to be detailed. Retained face holes are not counted as chassis fasteners.
Actual 3D sensor beam angles, printed strength, fastener preload, impact survival and cable bend radii remain unqualified.
The cradle is suitable for a simple flat print orientation; the compound-curved hood needs localized supports and is not claimed to be support-free or a simple two-setup CNC part.
